mainTopic: A natural increase in the returned property, a will found on a dead man's thigh, and a שכיב מרע who says 'write and give'
overview: The גמרא first explains why the other brothers do not have to share with the man in question: the brother who recognized him is really claiming money for someone else. Next it quotes the משנה's rule that if the man in question dies, the property goes back to the brother who gave it. רבא asks who gets growth that is part of the land, like a thicker tree or new soil, and the question ends in a תיקו. A new משנה teaches that a will found tied to a dead man's thigh does nothing, but a will handed over through another person is valid. The גמרא defines a דייתיקי and a gift by their wording, and אביי explains which gift of a healthy person works like a שכיב מרע's gift. Then it discusses a שכיב מרע who said 'write and give a מנה' and died, and proves that רבי אלעזר said this ruling. רב דימי explains רבי יוחנן's 'תיבדק': we write only if the document was meant as proof. The amud ends by asking what such a case looks like, and the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Why the other brothers do not have to pay
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא keeps the rule that 'I don't know' is not enough to avoid paying. But it says our case is different, because the claim is really being made for someone else.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, I will tell you: someone who answers 'I don't know' is obligated to pay. But here it is different, because it is like saying 'another person has a מנה in your hand.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its earlier question: why don't the other brothers have to share with the man in question if they only say 'we don't know'? It explains that this case is not like a normal claim.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, when someone says 'you owe me a מנה' and the other side answers 'I don't know,' the one answering must pay. Here, though, the brother who recognized the man is not claiming money for himself. He is like someone claiming that a third person is owed money, and against that kind of claim, 'I don't know' is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, I will tell you (I am keeping the original rule)
Here it is different
Another person has a מנה in your hand: a claim made on someone else's behalf
Obligated (to pay)

steps.whatToRemember: Saying 'I don't know' does not free you when someone claims money for himself. It does free you when he is claiming for someone else.

phrases.english: Really, I will tell you: he is obligated;
phrases.notes: This is the one who answers 'I don't know' to the claim 'you owe me a מנה.' The גמרא keeps that rule.

phrases.english: but here it is different,
because it is like saying "another person has a מנה in your hand."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge raised just before this section, which compared our case to the 'מנה לי בידך / איני יודע' case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case (שאני הכא): the claim is made on another person's behalf
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The other brothers, who say 'we don't know,' should have to pay like any 'I don't know' answer.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule stays, but here the claim is made for another person, so 'I don't know' is enough.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: if he dies, the property goes back
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the line in the משנה about what happens when the man in question dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he died, the property goes back to its place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה. It is setting up רבא's question, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man in question received a share only from the brother who recognized him. So when he dies, that property goes back to that brother, not to all the brothers.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall go back
Property
To their place (to where they came from)

phrases.english: If he died, the property shall go back to its place.
phrases.notes: The property goes back to the brother who recognized him, since it came out of that brother's share.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the brothers' claims to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the man in question dies, the property he received goes back to the brother who gave it.

steps.title: רבא asks about a natural increase in the property
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks who gets the extra value when the property grew on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: if the property increased in value on its own, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks a question about the משנה's rule. If the property grew in value by itself, does the increase also go back to the brother who gave it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the property goes back, but it does not say what happens to growth that came without any work. Does that growth count as part of the original property, which goes back to the one brother? Or does it count as new property, which all the brothers share?

keyTerms.meaning: He asked (raised a question)
Increase in value
On their own, without work
What is the law?

phrases.english: Rava asked:
an increase that the property gained on its own,
what is the law?
phrases.notes: In other words, who gets the increase: the brother who recognized him, or all the brothers?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a detail the משנה just quoted did not explain.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a natural increase go back with the property, or is it shared by all the brothers?

steps.title: Narrowing the question to growth that is still part of the land
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says crops that are ready to harvest are clearly not part of the question. The question is only about growth that is still attached to the land, like a thicker tree or new soil.
steps.simpleTranslation: About an increase that 'reaches the shoulders,' don't ask, because it is like property that came to him from somewhere else. Ask about an increase that does not reach the shoulders: for example, a palm tree that got thicker, or land that built up new soil. What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes רבא's question narrower. It explains which kind of increase is clearly not in doubt, and which kind really is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Crops ready to be carried off count as separate new property, so they are shared like property from elsewhere. The real doubt is about growth that becomes part of the land itself, like a thicker trunk or new soil. That kind of growth might go back to the brother who gave the land.

keyTerms.meaning: That reaches the shoulders: produce ready to harvest and carry
Don't ask about this
When you should ask
Palm tree
New soil (silt) that builds up on land

steps.confusionAlert: 'Reaches the shoulders' does not mean tall. It means the produce is ready to be picked and carried away on the shoulders.

phrases.aramaic: בְּשֶׁבַח הַמַּגִּיעַ לַכְּתֵפַיִם – לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ,
phrases.english: About an increase that reaches the shoulders, don't ask,

phrases.aramaic: דְּכִי נָפְלוּ לוֹ נְכָסִים מִמָּקוֹם אַחֵר דָּמֵי.
phrases.english: because it is like property that came to him from somewhere else.
phrases.notes: The משנה said property from elsewhere is shared by all the brothers.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ – בְּשֶׁבַח שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַגִּיעַ לַכְּתֵפַיִם;
phrases.english: Where you should ask is about an increase that does not reach the shoulders;
for example, a palm tree that got thicker,
or land that built up new soil;
what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּשֶׁבַח הַמַּגִּיעַ לַכְּתֵפַיִם לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Makes רבא's question narrower and clearer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does growth that becomes part of the land go back with the land, or is it shared like new property?

steps.title: The question stays unanswered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא leaves רבא's question unanswered.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand (unanswered).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the discussion without an answer. רבא's question remains open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No source settles whether growth attached to the land counts as part of the original property. So the question is left as a תיקו.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand: the question is left unanswered

steps.whatToRemember: Crops ready to harvest are shared by all the brothers, like property from elsewhere. Growth that is part of the land, like a thicker tree or new soil, is left as an open question (תיקו).

phrases.english: Let it stand unanswered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question without solving it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The case of natural growth that is part of the land stays undecided.

steps.title: A will tied to a dead man's thigh is worth nothing
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: if a man dies and a will is found tied to his thigh, it has no effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone died, and a will was found tied to his thigh. This is nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It says that a will found on a dead man's body does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though it is clearly his own will, he never gave it to anyone. Since it was never handed over, nobody received the property through it.

keyTerms.meaning: משנה (start of a new משנה)
A will written by a sick person before he dies
His thigh
It is nothing (has no effect)

phrases.english: משנה:
Someone who died, and a will was found
tied to his thigh:
this is nothing.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁמֵּת וְנִמְצֵאת דְּיָיתֵיקֵי קְשׁוּרָה עַל יְרֵיכוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A will that was never handed over to anyone has no effect.

steps.title: A will handed over through another person is valid
steps.stepSummary: If he gave ownership through another person, whether an heir or not, the will stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he gave ownership of it through another person, whether that person is one of the heirs or not one of the heirs, his words stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה goes on: if the man transferred the will through someone else, it does work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What makes the will work is that it was actually handed over through a person. It does not matter whether that person is an heir or not.

keyTerms.meaning: He gave ownership (transferred)
The heirs
His words stand (are valid)

steps.whatToRemember: A will must be handed over to work. If it is just found on his body, it does nothing. If it was transferred through another person, it is valid.

phrases.english: If he gave ownership of it through another person,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין מִן הַיּוֹרְשִׁין, בֵּין שֶׁאֵינָן מִן הַיּוֹרְשִׁין –
phrases.english: whether one of the heirs or not one of the heirs,
his words stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite case to step 6: a will that was handed over works.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A will transferred through another person, heir or not, is valid.

steps.title: A ברייתא defines a will and a gift by their wording
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: a דייתיקי says 'this shall stand and exist,' and a מתנה says 'from today and after death.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: What counts as a will (דייתיקי)? Any document that says, 'This shall stand and exist.' What counts as a gift? Any document that says, 'From today and after death.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining the משנה by bringing a ברייתא that defines a דייתיקי and a מתנה by the words written in each document.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה spoke about a דייתיקי found on a dead man's thigh, so the גמרא first defines what a דייתיקי is. The ברייתא says the exact wording decides the type of document. A will uses the phrase 'to stand and exist,' and a gift uses the phrase 'from today and after death.'

keyTerms.meaning: A will that takes effect after the writer's death
To stand and to exist: the wording of a will
From today and after death: the wording of this gift

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Sages taught:
Which is a dayetikei?
phrases.notes: This is the will mentioned in the משנה, the one found tied to the dead man's thigh.

phrases.english: Any document in which it is written:
'This shall be to stand and to exist.'
And which is a gift?
Any document in which it is written: 'From today and after death.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the term דייתיקי used in the משנה of steps 6-7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A דייתיקי says 'this shall stand and exist'; a מתנה says 'from today and after death.'

steps.title: Is a gift only valid with 'from today and after death'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: does a document that just says 'from now' not count as a gift?
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it only 'from today and after death' that makes a gift? Is a document that says 'from now' not a gift?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the ברייתא's definition of a gift, because it seems to leave out the simplest kind of gift.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא made it sound like a gift needs the wording 'from today and after death.' But a plain gift saying 'from now' is obviously a gift too. So the definition seems too narrow.

keyTerms.meaning: From now: an ordinary gift that takes effect right away
It is / it counts as

phrases.english: But is it only 'from today and after death'
that is a gift,
while 'from now' is not a gift?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא ״מֵהַיּוֹם וּלְאַחַר מִיתָה״ – הוּא דְּהָוְיָא מַתָּנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא's definition of a gift in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's definition of a מתנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A plain 'from now' gift is clearly a gift, so the ברייתא cannot mean that only 'from today and after death' counts as a gift.

steps.title: אביי: the ברייתא means a healthy person's gift that works like a deathbed gift
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the ברייתא is describing a healthy person's gift that, like a שכיב מרע's gift, is acquired only after death.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said, this is what it means: Which gift of a healthy person is like the gift of a שכיב מרע, which is acquired only after death? Any document that says, 'From today and after death.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge by reading the ברייתא differently: it is not defining every gift, only one special kind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא was never saying that 'from now' is not a gift. It is asking which healthy person's gift is similar to a שכיב מרע's gift, where the receiver acquires only after death. The answer is a document that says 'from today and after death.'

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means: rereads a source
A gift given by a healthy person
A person on his deathbed
Acquires

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, the ברייתא is about a healthy person's gift written 'from today and after death,' which is acquired only after death like a שכיב מרע's gift. A plain 'from now' gift is still a full gift.

phrases.english: Abaye said, this is what it is saying:
Which is the gift of a healthy person
that is like the gift of a person on his deathbed,
in that he acquires only after death?
Any document in which it is written: 'From today and after death.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9 by rereading the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא defines every valid gift, so 'from now' would not count.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא only describes a healthy person's gift that works like a שכיב מרע's gift, acquired after death.

steps.title: A deathbed order to 'write and give' does not work after death
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא reports in the name of רבי יוחנן: if a שכיב מרע says 'write and give a מנה to someone' and dies, we do not write and give, since he may have meant to transfer only through a שטר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא sat in the porch of the study hall and said in the name of רבי יוחנן: A שכיב מרע who said, 'Write and give a מנה to so-and-so,' and then died, we do not write and give. Maybe he decided to transfer it only through a שטר, and a שטר cannot be made after death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: a ruling of רבי יוחנן about a dying man who orders a document to be written but dies before it is written.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a שכיב מרע's spoken words are enough to give a gift. But here he said 'write,' so maybe he wanted the gift to happen only through a שטר. Since he died before it was written, a שטר made now would be too late.

keyTerms.meaning: A porch or covered balcony
In the name of
Write and give
A sum of one hundred דינרים
He decided to transfer ownership

steps.confusionAlert: The problem is not that a שכיב מרע's words never work. The problem is that by saying 'write,' he may have made the gift depend on a שטר, and that שטר can no longer be written.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna was sitting
in the porch of the study hall,
and he sat and said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
A person on his deathbed who said,
'Write and give a maneh to so-and-so,'
and he died, we do not write and give;

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמָּא לֹא גָּמַר לְהַקְנוֹתוֹ אֶלָּא בִּשְׁטָר,
phrases.english: perhaps he decided to transfer it only through a document,
and there is no document after death.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵיב רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא בְּאַכְסַדְרָא דְּבֵי רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about a שכיב מרע's instruction to write a document.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If a שכיב מרע says 'write and give' and dies before the שטר is written, we do not write and give, because he may have meant to transfer only through a שטר.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר tells everyone to take care with this ruling
steps.stepSummary: In this version, רבי אלעזר endorses רבי יוחנן's ruling, telling the others to be careful with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said to them: Take care with it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר רב הונא adds that רבי אלעזר backed up רבי יוחנן's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'take care with it' means 'this ruling is right, hold on to it.' This adds a second Sage's support to the rule from the last step.

keyTerms.meaning: Take care with it: hold on to this ruling, it is correct

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said to them:
Take care with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: אִיזְדְּהַרוּ בַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds רבי אלעזר's endorsement of רבי יוחנן's ruling in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר confirms that the ruling of step 11 is correct.

steps.title: רב שיזבי swaps who said it and who approved it
steps.stepSummary: רב שיזבי reports the reverse: רבי אלעזר said the ruling, and רבי יוחנן told them to take care with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שיזבי said: רבי אלעזר said it, and רבי יוחנן said to them: Take care with it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שיזבי gives a different version of the story, switching who said the ruling and who approved it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling itself stays the same in both versions. The only change is the names: in רב שיזבי's version, רבי אלעזר is the author and רבי יוחנן is the one who endorses it.

keyTerms.meaning: He said it: he is the author of the ruling

steps.whatToRemember: Both versions agree on the ruling: a שכיב מרע who says 'write and give' and dies before the שטר is written gets no gift through it. They only argue about who said it and who approved it.

phrases.english: Rav Sheizevi said:
Rabbi Elazar said it,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲמַר לְהוּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אִיזְדְּהַרוּ בַּהּ.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yochanan said to them: Take care with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שֵׁיזְבִי אָמַר: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמְרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternate version of who said and who endorsed the ruling of steps 11-12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ruling is attributed to רבי אלעזר, with רבי יוחנן endorsing it.

steps.title: Logic shows that רבי אלעזר said the ruling
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says רב שיזבי's version makes more sense. A student vouches for his teacher's ruling, not the other way around.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: רב שיזבי's version makes sense. If רבי אלעזר said the ruling, it is natural that רבי יוחנן would vouch for it. But if רבי יוחנן said it, would רבי אלעזר need to vouch for his own teacher?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now chooses between the two versions from the last two steps. רב נחמן בר יצחק says רב שיזבי's version is the right one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן was רבי אלעזר's teacher. A teacher's ruling needs no support from his student, but a student's ruling can be strengthened when his teacher vouches for it. So the version where רבי יוחנן says 'be careful with it' about רבי אלעזר's ruling is the one that fits.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / it is reasonable
To vouch for it / to back up someone's ruling
His teacher
It is understandable if you say (sets up a 'but if...' comparison)

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
It is reasonable to follow Rav Sheizevi's version.
phrases.notes: This is the version from step 13, where רבי אלעזר said the ruling and רבי יוחנן told them to be careful with it.

phrases.aramaic: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אַמְרַהּ,
phrases.english: It makes sense if you say Rabbi Elazar said it,

phrases.aramaic: אִצְטְרִיךְ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְאַסְהוֹדֵי עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר.
phrases.english: that Rabbi Yoḥanan needed to vouch for Rabbi Elazar's ruling.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אַמְרַהּ,
phrases.english: But if you say Rabbi Yoḥanan said it,
would Rabbi Elazar need to vouch
for the ruling of Rabbi Yoḥanan, his own teacher?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between the two versions given in steps 12 and 13
steps.raayaObject: רב שיזבי's version: רבי אלעזר said the ruling
steps.raayaSupportSource: Logic: a teacher vouches for his student, not a student for his teacher

steps.title: A letter to בבל proves that רבי אלעזר said the ruling
steps.stepSummary: A second proof: רבי אלעזר sent this ruling to בבל, and רבי יוחנן reacted to it separately by saying 'תיבדק'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And also, come and hear a proof that רבי אלעזר said it. רבין sent a message in the name of רבי אבהו: Know that רבי אלעזר sent to בבל in the name of our teacher: if a שכיב מרע said 'write and give a מנה to so-and-so' and died, we do not write and give. Perhaps he decided to transfer it only through a document, and a document does not work after death. And רבי יוחנן said: It should be checked.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second proof that רבי אלעזר is the one who said the ruling. It quotes a letter that he sent to the Jews in בבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the letter, רבי אלעזר is the one sending the ruling, and רבי יוחנן is quoted as reacting to it with 'תיבדק'. That matches רב שיזבי's version, where רבי אלעזר says the ruling and רבי יוחנן comments on it. The reason for the ruling is also spelled out: the dying man may have meant to give only through a document, and a document cannot take effect once the giver has died.

keyTerms.meaning: The exile, meaning the Jewish community in בָּבֶל
A person who is dangerously ill, on his deathbed
A sum of money, one hundred דִּינָרִים
A document cannot take effect after the giver dies
It should be checked / looked into

phrases.english: And furthermore, come and hear
that Rabbi Elazar was the one who said it,
for Ravin sent a message in the name of Rabbi Abbahu:
Know that Rabbi Elazar sent
to the exile, in the name of our teacher:
phrases.notes: 'The exile' means בבל, where many Jews lived outside ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: A person on his deathbed who said:
"Write and give a maneh to so-and-so," and then died,
we do not write and give;

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמָּא לֹא גָּמַר לְהַקְנוֹתוֹ אֶלָּא בִּשְׁטָר,
phrases.english: perhaps he decided to transfer it only through a document,
and a document does not work after death.
And Rabbi Yoḥanan said: It should be checked.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד, תָּא שְׁמַע דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אַמְרַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second proof, from a source, for the same conclusion as step 14
steps.raayaObject: רבי אלעזר is the one who said the ruling
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבין's report, in the name of רבי אבהו, of רבי אלעזר's letter to בבל, with רבי יוחנן's reply

steps.title: What does 'it should be checked' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי יוחנן meant by 'תיבדק'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'it should be checked' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רבי יוחנן's short reply means. This question sets up the explanation that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן did not say what should be checked or how. The גמרא needs to know whether he is disagreeing with רבי אלעזר or just adding a condition.

keyTerms.meaning: What is / what does it mean

phrases.english: What does "it should be checked" mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the last words of the letter quoted in step 15
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly must be checked, according to רבי יוחנן

steps.title: רב דימי explains: check the dying man's intention
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי explains that the court looks at what the שכיב מרע intended. If he only wanted to strengthen the recipient with written proof, we write; if not, we do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said: A later deathbed will cancels an earlier one. And: a שכיב מרע who said 'write and give a מנה to so-and-so' and died, we look into it. If it was a case of strengthening the recipient's position, we write. If not, we do not write.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי answers the question and explains what רבי יוחנן meant. He also brings a separate rule: a later deathbed will cancels an earlier one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'תיבדק' means the court must figure out why the dying man asked for a document. If the gift was already meant to happen through his words and the document was only extra proof, we write it even after his death. If he meant the gift to happen only through the document, it cannot be written once he has died.

keyTerms.meaning: A deathbed will
We look into it / the court assesses
Strengthening the recipient's position, by giving him written proof of the gift

steps.whatToRemember: A שכיב מרע's 'write and give' depends on his intention. If the document was only meant as proof, we write it. If the document was meant to be the way the gift is given, we do not, because a document cannot take effect after death.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not simply arguing with רבי אלעזר. רבי אלעזר's 'we do not write' still applies when the document was meant to make the gift. רבי יוחנן adds that when it was only meant as proof, we do write.

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said:
A dayetikei cancels a dayetikei.
phrases.notes: A דייתיקי is a deathbed will. This is a separate rule: a newer will cancels an older one.

phrases.english: A person on his deathbed who said:
"Write and give a maneh to so-and-so," and then died,
we look into it;
if it was like strengthening his position,
phrases.notes: He means the recipient: the document just gives him proof that the gift is his.

phrases.english: we write;
and if not, we do not write.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The court checks the giver's intention: if the document was to strengthen the recipient, write it; if the gift depended on the document, do not

steps.title: A ברייתא suggests a שכיב מרע's document is always written
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר ממל challenges the ruling from a ברייתא. The ברייתא says a healthy person's 'write and give' is not carried out, which implies a שכיב מרע's always is.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא בר ממל objected: A healthy person who said 'write and give a מנה to so-and-so' and died, we do not write and give. That implies that for a שכיב מרע, we do write and give!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא בר ממל raises a challenge from a ברייתא against the ruling that we sometimes do not write for a שכיב מרע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says 'we do not write' only about a healthy person. That suggests a שכיב מרע is different, and his document is written with no conditions. This clashes with רבי אלעזר's ruling and with רב דימי's 'if not, we do not write'.

keyTerms.meaning: A healthy person
This implies / but then (introduces an inference from the wording)

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba bar Memel raised an objection:
A healthy person who said:
"Write and give a maneh to so-and-so," and then died,
we do not write and give.
This implies that for a person on his deathbed, we do write and give!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling just explained in steps 15 and 17
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that a שכיב מרע's 'write and give' is sometimes not carried out
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Because the ברייתא limits 'we do not write' to a healthy person, it implies a שכיב מרע's instruction is always carried out

steps.title: The ברייתא is about a case where the document only strengthens the recipient
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר ממל answers his own challenge: the ברייתא's inference about a שכיב מרע is about a case where the document was only meant as proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: He raised the objection and he answered it: it is a case where he was strengthening the recipient's position.
steps.whatsHappening: The same חכם who asked the question now answers it. The ברייתא's inference applies only where the dying man wanted the document just as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a שכיב מרע only wanted to give written proof, his spoken words already gave the gift, so we write the document. A healthy person's words alone do not transfer anything, so even then nothing is written. This fits רב דימי's explanation, and the challenge is gone.

keyTerms.term: הוּא מוֹתֵיב לַהּ וְהוּא מְפָרֵק לַהּ
keyTerms.meaning: He raised the objection and he himself resolved it

steps.whatToRemember: Both the ברייתא and רבי יוחנן agree: a שכיב מרע's 'write and give' is carried out after his death only when the document was meant to strengthen the recipient, not to make the gift.

phrases.aramaic: הוּא מוֹתֵיב לַהּ וְהוּא מְפָרֵק לַהּ
phrases.english: He raised the objection and he resolved it:
It is a case where he was strengthening his position.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא מוֹתֵיב לַהּ וְהוּא מְפָרֵק לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 18
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the ברייתא's inference to a specific case (מיפה את כחו)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא implies every שכיב מרע's 'write and give' is carried out
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא's inference is only about a שכיב מרע who meant the document as proof, which fits רב דימי's explanation

steps.title: What case counts as strengthening the recipient's position?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a concrete example of a case where the שכיב מרע only wanted to strengthen the recipient with a document.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does a case of 'strengthening his position' look like?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a clear example of when a שכיב מרע is 'מְיַפֶּה אֶת כֹּחוֹ', strengthening the recipient's position. This question sets up the next move, and the גמרא describes the case on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps said a document is written only if the שכיב מרע meant it as extra proof for the recipient, not as the thing that makes the gift happen. But that is still a general idea. Now the גמרא wants to know how a court can tell, in a real case, that this was his intention.

keyTerms.meaning: What are the circumstances? What does the case look like? A request for a concrete example.
Strengthens his power. The document only gives the recipient extra backing and proof.
Power, legal strength or standing.

phrases.english: What are the circumstances
of 'enhancing his power'?
phrases.notes: This refers back to step 17: the שכיב מרע only wanted to give the recipient written backing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a concrete case to illustrate the 'only meant as proof' idea that resolved רבי אבא בר ממל's challenge in step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A concrete description of a case where it is clear that the שכיב מרע's instruction to write a document was only meant to strengthen the recipient, not to transfer the gift.
